answer: Agents trading onyx, saffron or tundra maps must solve a fresh hash puzzle before their key gains a vote each epoch. The puzzle includes an unpredictable beacon and that key; validators check the target and reject reused proofs. A thousand aliases need a thousand independent searches, so splitting one solution adds no votes. Difficulty sets a real computation cost per identity, while checking a proof needs one hash. Cheap electricity and specialized hardware still favor wealthy attackers.
